evidence.quote: API access requires a platform subscription plus a separate Direct Data contract, both quote-only.
Existing PitchBook platform customers start in the Plugins & Apps section of the Platform sidebar. New customers contact the Direct Data team directly.
The API uses API key or token-based authentication.
This API is a RESTFUL implementation that can be easily accessed by most HTTP clients in the language of your choosing.
no public endpoint reference, no OpenAPI spec, no interactive explorer
A developer cannot evaluate the API without first signing a contract.

result.notes: No self-serve signup exists: PitchBook's API is an enterprise add-on layered on top of an existing paid platform subscription, provisioned only after a separate quote-only "Direct Data" contract; new prospects are routed to sales rather than a signup page. Official docs (pitchbook.com/help/PitchBook-api) returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch (consistent with precomputed docs_page probe), so primary-source content came from Google's indexed snippet plus third-party writeups. Interestingly, a machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.1 spec is reachable at https://api.pitchbook.com/api-docs (the precomputed openapi_spec_found_at hint) and shows a custom "pbToken" security scheme on every endpoint, covering companies, deals, people, investors, funds, service providers, limited partners, and patents — this contradicts one third-party claim that "no OpenAPI spec" exists publicly, though the spec alone is useless without a contracted pbToken. A sandbox environment can be requested from the account manager, but only for already-contracted customers, not prospective developers. No MCP server (official or community) or Composio integration found.
result.one_liner: PitchBook is a private-market financial data platform (companies, deals, investors, funds, LPs) offering a RESTful JSON API as a paid enterprise add-on.
